bridgeUrl.name: Vault address
bridgeUrl.hint: Where Tusk's Vault is listening on this machine. Leave blank to find it automatically — set it only if you run Vault on an unusual port. Stored per browser, not shared with players.

enabled.name: Enable in this world
enabled.hint: Turn the archivist off for this world without uninstalling the module.

askPolicy.name: Who may ask
askPolicy.hint: The lowest rank at which someone may put a question to the archivist. Named exceptions are added on top of this, in Chosen askers below.
askPolicy.nobody: Nobody by rank — only the chosen askers below

replyVisibility.name: Who sees the answer
replyVisibility.hint: Set separately from who may ask, so players can put questions to the archivist while you read the answers first. Whispering bounds who SEES an answer, not what a player can pull: the archive has no notion of what you have revealed yet.
replyVisibility.gm: The GM only — you decide what to share

allowList.name: Chosen askers
allowList.label: Choose who may ask
allowList.hint: Named people who may always ask, whatever their rank. Use this for a co-GM on a player account, or a single loremaster at an otherwise closed table.

triggerCommand.name: Chat command
triggerCommand.hint: Typed with a leading slash. The default gives you /tusk your question here.

botName.name: Archivist name
botName.hint: The name answers are posted under, and the @mention that also triggers a question.

connect.name: Connection
connect.label: Connect to Tusk's Vault
connect.hint: Find Tusk's Vault on this machine and pair with it. You will be shown a code to confirm in the Vault dashboard.

answerSource.name: Where answers come from
answerSource.hint: Tusk's Vault is the full experience and it is free — this module is its Foundry end. Lite is a cut-down archivist that runs inside Foundry alone, for trying the idea before installing anything.

liteFolder.name: Lore folder
liteFolder.hint: Lite mode reads the journal pages in this folder and its subfolders, and nothing else. Each page is one source, cited by its own name. Which pages may be used to answer whom is decided by “Lite: what each answer may draw on”, below.

liteAnswers.name: Lite: write answers, not just find passages
liteAnswers.hint: Off, lite searches your journals and quotes what it finds — no key, no network, no cost. On, it also needs a Gemini key on the GM's browser and writes a prose answer. Read the note under Gemini key before turning this on.

liteModel.name: Lite: Gemini model
liteModel.hint: Lite uses Gemini flash and flash-lite, version 3 and above. Leave this alone unless you want a specific one — if Google retires the model, lite finds a replacement by itself and updates this. Use Choose from available models to pick, or TusksVault.models() in the F12 console to look.

liteKey.name: Gemini key (lite mode)
liteKey.label: Set the Gemini key
liteKey.hint: Needed only for lite answers. Stored in this browser alone, never in the world, never shown to players. Explains what it can and cannot protect before it takes anything.

liteModelPicker.name: Model
liteModelPicker.label: Choose from available models
liteModelPicker.hint: Lists the flash and flash-lite models your key can reach right now, newest first. Fetched live, so it is never out of date.

liteFilters.name: Lite: apply Google's content filters
liteFilters.hint: Off by default, and off is what Tusk's Vault does too. A campaign archive gets asked about war, murder and worse because that is what your notes are about, and a filtered refusal reads as the archive not knowing rather than declining. Turn this on if your table wants Google's standard filtering — remember answers land in a chat log everyone reads.

liteWhyUpgrade.name: The full version
liteWhyUpgrade.label: Why move up to Tusk's Vault
liteWhyUpgrade.hint: A side-by-side of what lite does and what the full application does. Tusk's Vault is free.

liteScope.name: Lite: what each answer may draw on
liteScope.hint: By default Tusk reads everything in your lore folders, whoever is asking — what you put in the folder is what it may say. The other two read Foundry's journal ownership instead, which only works if you keep those permissions up to date.
liteScope.shared: Only what every player can open
liteScope.asker: Only what the person asking can open — experimental

about.name: About Tusk's Vault
about.label: About, and getting help
about.hint: Version, links, a diagnostics report you can paste into a bug report, and how to support the project.

lorePermissions.name: Lite: review lore permissions
lorePermissions.label: Check who can read what
lorePermissions.hint: Lists every page in your lore folder and who at the table can be answered from it. Useful before you let players add their own notes.

liteFolders.name: Lite: also read these folders
liteFolders.label: Pick journal folders
liteFolders.hint: Read the journal folders you already have, instead of moving your notes into a new one.

faq.name: Common questions
faq.label: Open the FAQ
faq.hint: The questions people actually ask, each with a link to the answer in full.

pairing.title: Pair with Tusk's Vault
pairing.body: Open the Tusk's Vault dashboard. It is showing a pairing request with a code — check it matches the one below, then click Allow.
pairing.hint: If the codes do not match, click Deny: something else asked to connect.

allowList.title: Chosen askers
allowList.body: Anyone ticked here may ask the archivist whatever their rank. This is added to the rank you set in Who may ask — it never takes access away.
allowList.hint: With Who may ask set to "Nobody by rank", this list becomes the whole policy: a GM who is not ticked cannot ask either.
allowList.empty: This world has no users yet.

liteKey.title: Gemini key for lite mode
liteKey.body: Lite mode can write prose answers using Google's Gemini, which has a free tier. The key is stored in this browser only — never in the world, so no player at your table can read it.
liteKey.riskHead: Before you paste one, three things worth knowing:
liteKey.riskModules: Foundry does not sandbox modules. Every other module you have installed runs on this page and can read this browser's storage — including this key. Only install modules you trust.
liteKey.riskPlayers: Your players cannot read it, and it is never sent to the Foundry server. It goes from this browser straight to Google.
liteKey.riskCap: Use a key made for this and nothing else, and set a spending cap on it in Google's console. That turns the worst case from an open tab into a fixed number.
liteKey.riskFull: Tusk's Vault keeps the key off the browser entirely. It is free, and this is the main reason to move up to it once you have decided you like this.
liteKey.present: A key is set in this browser ({length} characters). Type a new one to replace it.
liteKey.absent: No key is set in this browser.
liteKey.where: Get a free key at aistudio.google.com/apikey

model.title: Choose a Gemini model
model.body: {allowed} of the {total} models your key can reach are flash or flash-lite, version 3 or above. Newest first.
model.note: Flash is the quality end and flash-lite the cheap, fast end. If the one you pick is later retired, lite moves to the newest available on its own.

why.title: Lite, and the full Tusk's Vault
why.body: Lite runs inside Foundry so you can try the idea without installing anything. Tusk's Vault is the whole application, it is free and open source, and this module is its Foundry end.
why.note: Both are MIT licensed. Moving up costs nothing but a download, and this module keeps working — you switch it to Tusk's Vault at the top of these settings.

lore.label: Where your lore lives
lore.lite: Journal entries you paste into one folder
lore.vault: The notes you already keep — Word documents, PDFs, Markdown, or a whole Obsidian vault

size.label: How much it can read
size.lite: Only what fits into a single question
size.vault: Everything you have, however much that is

finding.label: Finding the right note
finding.vault: Works out what you meant, so it still finds the page when you word it differently

paying.label: Paying for answers
paying.vault: An API key, a Claude Code subscription you may already pay for, or a local model for nothing

providers.label: Models
providers.vault: Claude, Gemini, Deepseek, Grok and 400+ more through OpenRouter

gaps.label: When it does not know
gaps.vault: Records the gap so you can answer it, and remembers your answer

why.tomes: Tusk's Tomes — turn recordings into lore
why.loopHead: Where the lore comes from in the first place.
why.loopBody: Record your session and Tusk's Tomes turns the recording into a written chronicle and a session log. Those land in the same folder Tusk's Vault reads, so by the next session the archive can already answer questions about what just happened — without you writing a word of it up. Tomes writes the history, Vault remembers it, and the table asks it questions.

about.title: About Tusk's Vault
about.blurb: Ask your campaign's own lore from the chat bar, and get an answer cited to the note it came from.
about.modeLite: Lite — journal entries in this world
about.helpBody: Copy the diagnostics report and paste it into your bug report. It records shapes, never values — no question text, no answer text, no key, no world name.
about.copyFailed: Could not reach the clipboard. Press F12 and run TusksVault.diagnostics() instead.
about.supportBody: Tusk's Vault is free, open source, and stays that way. If it has saved you some prep time, you are welcome to put something in the tip jar — but please do not feel you need to.

perms.title: Who can be answered from what
perms.body: Every page in {folder}, and which players Lite may use it to answer. This is Foundry's own journal ownership — change it on the entry or the page, not here.
perms.empty: No readable pages found in {folder}. Make the folder in the Journals sidebar and put notes in it, or point the lore folder setting somewhere else.
perms.writable: {count} player(s) can create journal entries, so notes may appear here that you did not write.

setup.title: Tusk's Vault — pick how it answers
setup.body: Tusk answers questions about your campaign from your own notes, in chat. There are two ways to run it, and you can change your mind at any time in Module Settings.
setup.liteBody: Answers from journal entries in a folder called “{folder}” in this world. No account, no API key, no network request. Best place to start: put some notes in the folder and ask a question.
setup.bridgeBody: Answers from the notes you already keep on your computer — Word, PDF, Markdown, a whole Obsidian vault — on whichever model you like, with your API key kept out of the browser. It is free, but it is a separate download you run yourself.
setup.either: Not sure? Start with Lite. Moving up later costs nothing but a download, and this module keeps working — you switch it at the top of the module settings.

folders.title: Which journal folders should Tusk read?
folders.body: Tick any folders you already keep notes in. Tusk reads them alongside your lore folder, including anything nested inside them — so you do not have to move or retype anything.
folders.primary: Always read: “{folder}”, plus everything nested inside it.
folders.noPrimary: Your lore folder “{folder}” does not exist yet. Anything you tick here is read on its own.
folders.none: There are no other journal folders in this world yet.
folders.note: Journal permissions still apply. Ticking a folder does not show anyone anything they could not already open.

faq.title: Tusk's Vault — common questions
faq.body: The things people ask most. Open one for the short answer, or follow the link for the whole story.
faq.footer: Still stuck? The troubleshooting page lists every error code and what fixes it — and the About screen has a diagnostics report you can paste into a bug report.

notify.gmOnlyPairing: Only a GM can pair this world with Tusk's Vault.
notify.gmOnlyAllowList: Only a GM can change who may ask.
notify.allowListFailed: Could not save the chosen askers: {detail}
notify.allowListUnavailable: This Foundry version cannot show the picker. Set Who may ask to a rank instead.
notify.searching: Looking for Tusk's Vault on this machine…
notify.notFound: Could not find Tusk's Vault. It must be running on this same computer, and it answers on ports {range}. If you started it on a different port, put that address in the module setting "Vault address" and try again.
notify.protocolMismatch: Tusk's Vault {version} speaks a different bridge protocol than this module. Update Tusk's Vault, then pair again.
notify.pairFailed: Tusk's Vault refused the pairing request.
notify.paired: Paired with Tusk's Vault. Try asking something in chat.
notify.askSomething: Ask a question — for example, /{command} who runs the harbour?
notify.dialogFailed: That screen could not be opened. Reload Foundry, and if it keeps happening use Copy diagnostics on the About screen when reporting it.
notify.modelMovedOnce: Google no longer offers {from}, so Tusk used {to} for this answer. The saved setting could not be updated — change it under Module Settings to make it stick.
notify.noActiveGM: No GM is connected, so there is nobody to reach the archive. Ask again once a GM is online.
notify.needsPairing: Tusk's Vault is not paired yet. Open the Settings sidebar → Game Settings → Module Settings → Tusk's Vault → Connect.
notify.pairError: Pairing did not finish: {detail} Tusk's Vault may now list this world as paired even though Foundry has no token — pair again.
notify.triggerFailed: Tusk's Vault could not handle that command: {detail}
notify.pairExpired: The pairing request expired before it was approved. Click Connect and try again.
notify.pairedButUnusable: Paired, but Tusk's Vault would not answer: {detail}
notify.gmOnlyKey: Only a GM can set the Gemini key.
notify.keySaved: Gemini key saved in this browser.
notify.keyCleared: Gemini key removed from this browser.
notify.keyUnchanged: Nothing typed — the key is unchanged. Use Remove the key to clear it.
notify.modelMoved: {from} is no longer available. Lite has moved to {to} and saved it.
notify.noAllowedModels: None of the {count} models your key can reach are flash or flash-lite version 3 or above. Set the model by hand, or check your Google project.
notify.liteKeyMissingHere: Lite answers are on for this world, but this browser has no Gemini key — so questions are being searched, not answered. The key is stored per browser: set it here under Module Settings, or ask whichever GM has it to be the one online.
notify.scopeUnreadable: Tusk's Vault: answers read your whole lore folder whoever asks, so {count} page(s) your players cannot open in Foundry may still be quoted to them. That is what “Everything in the lore folders” means, not a fault — but if you would rather Tusk followed the permissions you already set, switch “what each answer may draw on” to one of the other two.
notify.scopeWideOpen: Tusk's Vault: answers read your whole lore folder whoever asks, and {count} entrie(s) in it can be edited by a player. Text in the folder goes into the prompt, so a note a player writes sits beside lore they cannot read. Move those entries out, or switch “what each answer may draw on” to a per-player setting.
notify.setupLiteMade: Lite is on, and a journal folder called “{folder}” has been created. Put some notes in it, then type /{command} followed by a question.
notify.setupLiteReady: Lite is on, reading the journal folder “{folder}”. Type /{command} followed by a question.
notify.foldersSaved: Tusk now also reads {count} extra journal folder(s).
notify.scopePreserved: Tusk's Vault 1.1.0 adds a setting for what each answer may draw on. This world has been left on the behaviour it already had — each person answered only from journal pages they can open. New worlds read the whole lore folder instead. Change it under Module Settings if you would rather.

chat.hintRepair: If you have started opening Foundry on a different address — a LAN IP instead of localhost, or https instead of http — the pairing was tied to the old one. Open the module settings and use “Connect to Tusk's Vault” to pair again.
chat.hintUnreachable: Tusk's Vault does not appear to be running on this computer. Start it, then ask again.
chat.notPermitted: The archivist does not take questions from you at this table. Your GM sets who may ask.
chat.answeredToGM: Your question went to the GM, who will answer at the table.
chat.notConnected: Tusk's Vault is not paired with this world yet. Open the Settings sidebar → Game Settings → Module Settings → Tusk's Vault → Connect.
chat.notConnectedAsker: The archive is not connected yet — your GM needs to finish setting up Tusk's Vault.
chat.unreachable: Tusk's Vault is not answering at {address}. Check it is running on the GM's machine.
chat.timedOut: Tusk's Vault did not answer in time.
chat.askBusy: Tusk is still working on your last question. Wait for that answer before asking another.
chat.askQueue: Tusk is already answering several questions. Try again in a moment.
chat.narrowedPublicly: Answered privately — this one draws on notes not everyone can open.
chat.answeredPrivately: Answered privately rather than to the table: this draws on notes not everyone can open.

lite.noMatches: I am unsure about this detail. Nothing in your lore folder mentions it.
lite.noFolder: Lite mode found no lore to read. Make a journal folder called "{folder}" and put your notes in it, or point the Lore folder setting somewhere else. Tusk's Vault reads the documents you already keep on disk instead, and is free: {site}
lite.noAnswer: Gemini returned nothing ({reason}). Try rephrasing, or check the model name in module settings.
lite.gmOnly: Lite mode answers from the GM's browser, and this client is not a GM.
lite.noKey: No Gemini key is set in this browser.
lite.footer: That is lite mode quoting your notes. Tusk's Vault reads everything you keep, answers in prose and cites it, and is free.
lite.footerNoKey: Written answers are switched on for this table, but the GM answering has no Gemini key saved in their browser — a key is stored per browser, not in the world.
lite.timedOut: Google did not answer in time. The question may be too large, or the connection slow — try again, or ask something narrower.
lite.offline: Could not reach Google from this browser. Check this computer's internet connection; Foundry itself is fine, or you would not be reading this.
lite.corpusDropped: Read {included} of {considered} matching notes — the rest did not fit into one question.
lite.corpusTruncated: One long note did not fit in full, so only the passage around your question was read.

notCommand.q: Foundry says /tusk is not a valid command
notCommand.a: Either the module is not switched on for this world, or the command has been renamed. Check Settings → Module Management, then Chat command in this module's settings.

nothing.q: I ask a question and nothing comes back
nothing.a: Questions are answered by the GM's browser, so a GM has to be logged in. If you are the GM and it is still silent, open About and copy the diagnostics report.

noMatches.q: It says it cannot find anything, but I know the note is there
noMatches.a: Without an API key Tusk matches the words you typed, letter for letter — it has no notion of what they mean. “harbours” will not find “harbour”, and “wharf” or “quayside” will not find “harbour master”. Ask using the words your notes actually use. Also check the note is in a folder Tusk reads.

otherFolder.q: My notes are already in other folders. Do I have to move them?
otherFolder.a: No. Use “Lite: also read these folders” and tick the folders you already keep notes in. Nothing moves and nothing is copied.

players.q: Do my players need to install anything?
players.a: No. Players install nothing and set nothing up. They type a question in chat like anyone else.

key.q: Do I need an API key?
key.a: Not to use it. Without a key Tusk quotes the matching passages back at you, cited. A free Gemini key turns those into written answers instead.

keySafe.q: Can my players see my API key?
keySafe.a: No. It is stored in your browser only, never in the world, and never sent to the Foundry server. Other Foundry modules you install can read it, though — Foundry does not sandbox modules — so use a key made for this and set a spending cap.

spoilers.q: Will Tusk spoil things my players should not know?
spoilers.a: It answers from everything in your lore folders, whoever asks — so the folder is the boundary: do not put a secret in it you would not want surfaced. You can also restrict who may ask at all, or have answers whispered to you first. If you keep Foundry's journal permissions up to date, there is an experimental setting that reads them per player instead.

playerNotes.q: Can my players add their own lore, like backstories?
playerNotes.a: Yes, if you let them create journal entries. Note that by default every answer reads the whole folder, so what one player writes can be used to answer another. The experimental per-player setting is what keeps a backstory private to its author.

hosted.q: I run Foundry on The Forge or another host. Does this work?
hosted.a: Yes, both halves. Lite does not care where Foundry lives, and the full Vault runs on the computer you play from rather than on the server.

cost.a: Nothing to install and nothing to use without a key. If you add a Gemini key, Google's free tier is enough to try it, and you set your own spending cap.

difference.q: What is the difference between this and the full Tusk's Vault?
difference.a: This reads journal entries inside Foundry. The full version is a free app you run yourself that reads the notes you already keep — Word, PDF, Markdown, a whole Obsidian vault — on whichever model you like, with your key kept out of the browser.
